title: Regression: `macsec/test_docker_restart.py` preventing run_tests.py from running on T2 without a macsec enabled node.
author: arista-nwolfe
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Previous Working Version

Prior to https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/18518 merging

### Steps to Reproduce

Run run_tests.py on a T2 device with no macsec enabled nodes and the `pytest_generate_tests` will fail with:
`sudo ./run_tests.sh -n ardut -c test_pretest.py -x -e '--pdb'`
`ERROR macsec/test_docker_restart.py - AssertionError: Test selected require at-least one macsec node, none of the DUTs`

This is the assertion line:
```
assert len(frontend_duts) > 0, \
    "Test selected require at-least one {} node, " \
    "none of the DUTs '{}' in testbed '{}' are a {} node".format(host_type, duts, tbname, host_type)
```

From PDB I can see that it's this function check which prevents the node from being added to `frontend_duts`:
```
(Pdb) is_macsec_capable_node(inv_files, dut)
False
```

### Impact of this regression

Can't run `run_tests.sh` on a T2 without macsec enabled unless I first revert https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/18518

comments.author: augusdn
comments.body:
This behaviour is expected following the changes introduced in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/18518. The intent of that update was to ensure MACSec tests only run on devices that are both MACSec-capable and explicitly marked as such in the inventory file using the macsec_card = True flag.

The failure you're seeing:
`AssertionError: Test selected require at-least one macsec node, none of the DUTs`
is triggered by the is_macsec_capable_node(inv_files, dut) check, which correctly returns False when the DUT is not marked as MACSec-enabled in the inventory. This is by design to avoid false failures on non-MACSec nodes, especially in T2 environments where MACSec support is not universal.

To resolve this, please ensure that:

The DUT in your testbed is MACSec-capable.
The inventory file includes macsec_card = True for that DUT.

As this change was not very user-friendly, I’ll add a comment to `def generate_params_frontend_hostname(request, macsec_only=False):` to clarify the need to set `macsec_card = True` in the inventory to avoid assertion failures.

comments.author: augusdn
comments.body: @judyjoseph, can I ask for your feedback on this code change, use of macsec only DUT fixture, which could lead to test failure for cases where we don't specify `macsec_card = True` in the inventory of DUT?

comments.author: arista-nwolfe
comments.body:
> This behaviour is expected following the changes introduced in [#18518](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/18518). The intent of that update was to ensure MACSec tests only run on devices that are both MACSec-capable and explicitly marked as such in the inventory file using the macsec_card = True flag.
> 
> The failure you're seeing: `AssertionError: Test selected require at-least one macsec node, none of the DUTs` is triggered by the is_macsec_capable_node(inv_files, dut) check, which correctly returns False when the DUT is not marked as MACSec-enabled in the inventory. This is by design to avoid false failures on non-MACSec nodes, especially in T2 environments where MACSec support is not universal.
> 
> To resolve this, please ensure that:
> 
> The DUT in your testbed is MACSec-capable. The inventory file includes macsec_card = True for that DUT.
> 
> As this change was not very user-friendly, I’ll add a comment to `def generate_params_frontend_hostname(request, macsec_only=False):` to clarify the need to set `macsec_card = True` in the inventory to avoid assertion failures.

Thanks for taking a look @augusdn the problem isn't that the `macsec/test_docker_restart.py` test fails on our non-macsec LC. The problem is that I'm not running `macsec/test_docker_restart.py` and it's still failing, I was just running `test_pretest.py`, note my `run_tests.py` command: `sudo ./run_tests.sh -n ardut -c test_pretest.py -x -e '--pdb'`

I agree preventing non-macsec SKUs/LCs from running macsec tests makes sense but we shouldn't prevent non-macsec SKUs/LCs from running all tests.

comments.author: arista-nwolfe
comments.body:
Also I'd argue that if there isn't a macsec capable card it should be a test skip, not an assertion
`ERROR macsec/test_docker_restart.py - AssertionError: Test selected require at-least one macsec node, none of the DUTs`

comments.author: augusdn
arista-nwolfe
comments.body:
> [@arista-nwolfe](https://github.com/arista-nwolfe) I see your point, and I agree it's a valid point to skip macsec tests when we don't set up/enable macsec.
> 
> I have raised a PR to mitigate this issue.
> 
> Basically, we will skip macsec tests for T2, when 'macsec_en' is not set. This flag is set, when we provide 'enable_macsec' as extra params.

Thanks https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/18725 fixes the issue
